As Charles Tyrrell navigates his upbringing in a toxic household dominated by his father's mercurial temperament, we see early indications of his character—marked by a deep attachment to his mother and an aversion to his father's oppressive nature. This dynamic creates a foundation for the conflict and turmoil that will follow, as Charles grapples with the legacy of his family and his quest for autonomy and understanding in a challenging environment.
